title: Run the impact-versus-effort matrix
objective: Place a high-reach workflow requiring an unverified custom connector.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: The 2x2 matrix makes prioritization visible and fast. It is a tool for directional agreement, not a calculator.

blocks.caption: Impact vs. effort quadrants
head: Quadrant
Impact
Effort
What to do
rows: Prime candidates for the first wave
Select one or two for deeper discovery and phasing
Keep for later; don't let them crowd out quick wins

blocks.x: Five steps, live with the customer

items: **Review the list** in the shared document.
**Score quickly:** high, medium, or low for impact and effort.
**Place on the grid** as text boxes or sticky notes.
**Highlight picks:** two or three quick wins and one or two bets, where appropriate. These counts are guidance, not a rule.
**Validate with the sponsor:** "Does this reflect where to start?"

blocks.x: Keep each use case's evidence and rationale next to the visual.
A matrix is not a numerical ROI calculation. New evidence can and should move a use case. Never hide a connector blocker to keep a favorite in the quick-win quadrant.
Score live with the customer, then validate the picks with the sponsor. The matrix ranks options; it is not an ROI model.

blocks.title: Running the matrix live
blocks.alt: Five steps for running the impact/effort matrix with the customer: review the list, score quickly, place each item on the grid, highlight the picks, and validate them with the sponsor.
